summary: Copies up to the available output space from a circular output window into a destination buffer, advancing window and output cursors and firing an optional callout before each copied segment. Handles circular wrap: when the write cursor reaches the window boundary it resets to the window base and repeats the copy for the wrapped remainder. A third argument of -5 marks a flush/termination marker that is cleared to 0 when data is actually copied.

Flush guard: if the segment is non-empty and a3 == -5, clear a3 to 0 so a flush marker on real data is not reported as an error.
Advance output accounting: a2[5] += segment length and a2[4] = remaining - segment length.

Flush guard repeated for the wrapped segment: if non-empty and a3 == -5, clear a3 to 0.
Advance output accounting for the wrapped segment: a2[5] += length and a2[4] -= length.
Callout repeated for the wrapped segment: invoke this+0x38(this+0x3C, source, length) when present and store its return into this+0x3C and a2[12].
Copy the wrapped segment as full dwords plus len & 3 tail bytes.
Persist cursors: store the advanced destination into a2[3] and the advanced window position into this+0x30.
Return a3, which is the original flush marker unless data was copied (in which case it is 0).
